solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sheet anchor

parts.note: a sheet anchor is a ship's emergency anchor or a mainstay; read literally it is something that holds a sheet of paper down

explanation.surface: A nautical term for the heavy spare anchor a ship carries.
explanation.walkthrough: A sheet anchor is a sailor's term for a last-resort anchor; the cryptic reading takes 'sheet' as a sheet of paper and 'anchor' as whatever stops it blowing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk weight sits on loose papers and holds them in place, literally anchoring the sheets.

clue.text: Wolves needing time to get all essential elements brought together

parts.note: wolves hunt in a group called a pack
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A football club needs time to bring together all the essential parts of its team.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, which makes the surface about sport; here it is simply a group of wolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal offered as a bundle combines every necessary component into one whole, as in a holiday or pay offer.

clue.text: Strong sign resistance will disappear

indicators.note: the letter for resistance is said to vanish from the word for sign, so it is taken out

parts.note: a portent is an omen or sign of things to come
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A strong omen suggests that opposition will fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerful and forceful, as a strong drink or argument is described.

clue.text: People telling stories turn coarse when drunk

indicators.note: being drunk makes things go awry, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Storytellers become vulgar once they have had a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges the ten letters of TURN COARSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled anecdotalists are those who entertain listeners by narrating tales.

clue.text: Lord soon found to be deficient

indicators.note: deficient means lacking something, here the final letter of the synonym for soon

parts.note: early can mean soon, before the expected time

explanation.surface: A nobleman is soon discovered to be lacking in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficient' cuts the last letter, Y, from EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking above a viscount, addressed as Lord.

clue.text: With divine protection Jules ruled

indicators.note: the deity wraps around and shields the author, so the name goes inside

parts.note: the divine is God
Jules Verne, the French science-fiction writer

explanation.surface: Jules reigned under heaven's protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With divine protection' says GOD surrounds VERNE, the surname of the novelist Jules Verne.
explanation.definitionFit: Controlled or presided over a country or people, as a monarch does.

clue.text: Whistle that is nominally shared by two quarrelling brothers

definitions.meaning: to make a thin piping sound, as on a pipe or whistle

definitions.text: nominally shared by two quarrelling brothers
definitions.meaning: Tweedledum and Tweedledee, the squabbling twins in Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, both have names that begin with this word

explanation.surface: A whistle whose name belongs to two feuding siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping a reedy tune counts as whistling; the brothers are the Carroll twins whose names share this opening.

clue.text: Austere type left out of a second eleven based in Glasgow

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the team name

parts.note: Celtic is a Glasgow football club, a team of eleven

explanation.surface: A self-denying player is dropped from a Glasgow reserve team.
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic is a Scottish football club based in Glasgow, and a football team fields eleven players; 'out of' drops the L.
explanation.definitionFit: An austere person practises severe self-discipline and shuns pleasures, like a hermit or monk.

clue.text: Play just right for any person in general

definitions.meaning: a comedy by Shakespeare set in the Forest of Arden

definitions.text: just right for any person in general
definitions.meaning: suiting whatever anyone prefers, with you as the generic person

explanation.surface: A drama that suits everybody perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means exactly as the listener wishes, and it is also the title of Shakespeare's pastoral comedy.

clue.text: I arrive looking untidy in holiday area

indicators.note: untidy suggests things are out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone turns up dishevelled at a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastal strip of southern France and northern Italy, a favourite resort region.

clue.text: A bridge player, Richard, and two fellow players filled with astonishment

parts.note: West is one of the four seats at a bridge table
Rick is a short form of Richard
East and North are the other bridge seats, abbreviated E and N

explanation.surface: A card player named Richard and his partners are amazed at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, so West's fellow players include E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcome by wonder or amazement; struck dumb with awe.

clue.text: Time's no good for holding in desire

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: the abbreviation for no good is said to hold the next word, which therefore goes inside

explanation.surface: Time is useless for keeping one's longing in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong longing or craving for something, as a noun.

clue.text: Sharpness shown by doctor — one deals with a lot of rubbish

definitions.text: one deals with a lot of rubbish

parts.note: an edge is keenness or sharpness, as in a blade's edge

explanation.surface: A doctor shows sharpness and deals with a lot of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' just sets the doctor beside the sharpness.
explanation.definitionFit: A scooping machine that clears mud and silt from riverbeds and harbours, handling plenty of muck.

clue.text: One winning nothing receiving embrace from French author

indicators.note: the zero takes the hug beside it, so the hug comes just before it

parts.note: a victor is one who wins
a hug is an embrace
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A champion with nothing gets a hug from a French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineteenth-century novelist who wrote Les Misérables and The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Chemical in area by northern river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, in northern England

explanation.surface: A chemical is found in the area by a river in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure flows through Wensleydale in Yorkshire; 'in' and 'by' are just link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrogen compound excreted in urine, made industrially for fertiliser.

clue.text: Engineers, excellent fellows needing time for tweaking

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
fine means excellent
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Engineers and other good fellows need time for fine adjustments.
explanation.definitionFit: Small improvements made to polish something, as when a design is adjusted and perfected.

clue.text: Curse those people in an organisation supposed to help motorists

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the motoring organisation's initials

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, a British breakdown service
them refers to those people

explanation.surface: Those people at a motoring rescue service are cursed.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, which rescues broken-down cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ban or denunciation, also something deeply loathed, like a solemn curse.

clue.text: Loveless emperor with a penetrating urge — to ____ Rome!

indicators.note: the shortened emperor and the a pierce the word for urge, sitting inside it

parts.note: to incite is to urge on

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so the emperor loses that letter

parts.note: Nero, the Roman emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: Nero, lacking affection, had a burning urge to set Rome on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank definition: Nero was said to have fiddled while Rome burned. 'Loveless' drops O (love in tennis) from the emperor's name, leaving NER.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn completely to ashes, as Nero was accused of doing to his capital.

clue.text: Body of animal under vehicle, cold

indicators.note: in a down clue the animal sits beneath the vehicle and cold, so it comes after them

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
an ass is a donkey, an animal

explanation.surface: An animal's body lies chilled beneath a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The dead body of a beast, especially one prepared for butchery.

clue.text: Odd bits of Sue's mail in house

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters are picked out of the words

explanation.surface: Bits of Sue's post are scattered around her home.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is British shorthand for a semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A home joined to one neighbouring dwelling by a shared wall, a semi-detached.

clue.text: Hair being swept up added to our charm

indicators.note: in a down clue, sweeping up turns the word upwards so it reads backwards

parts.note: a mane is a long mass of hair

explanation.surface: Hair swept up adds to our attractiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being swept up' reverses MANE to ENAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to captivate them and fill them with love, a verb.

clue.text: Shelter gaping with its roof off

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: yawning means gaping wide open

explanation.surface: A shelter left gaping open after its roof blew off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with its roof off' removes the top letter Y from YAWNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas canopy over a shop window or doorway that keeps off sun and rain.

clue.text: Slips of paper?

parts.note: slips here are mistakes, not pieces; errors in print are listed after publication

explanation.surface: Small pieces of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips' suggests scraps of paper, but here it means printing mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing mistakes corrected in a book, the Latin plural for errors.

clue.text: Snag having daughter untrained, needing support

parts.note: raw means inexperienced or untrained
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A problem arises with an inexperienced daughter who needs backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage or hitch that spoils an otherwise good thing.

clue.text: River — some deny that will rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the letters go backwards
some means a portion of the letters, a run inside the words

explanation.surface: Some deny that the river will rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read DENY THAT backwards and TYNE lies within; the Tyne flows through Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river of north-east England that runs through Newcastle to the North Sea.

clue.text: Move quickly in attempt to make pattern

indicators.note: the dash is put inside the attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to race is to move quickly

explanation.surface: Rushing an effort to create a design.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental stone openwork in Gothic windows, or any delicate interlacing design.

clue.text: Mythical beast — gosh! — inside a French home

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the exclamation sits inside the word for home

parts.note: in means at home
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: Gosh, a mythical creature inside a French house!
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary horse-like creature with a single horn on its forehead.

clue.text: Awful screamer keeping on, originator of gloom?

definitions.text: Awful screamer keeping on, originator of gloom?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the next pieces inside them
awful suggests something mangled, so these letters are rearranged
the originator of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful shrieker who keeps going on spreads gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges the screamer into SCAREMER, which 'keeping' wraps around the other pieces. The whole clue also describes the answer: a shrieking doom-monger.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who spreads alarming rumours and fear, an alarmist.
